results.name: Reverse Machine Fly
instructions: Sit on a stool with your back straight, knees bent, and feet on the floor.
Extend your arms forward and grab the handles of the machine with your palms facing down.
Pull the handles by opening your arms wide to your sides.
As your arms are aligned with the shoulders, return to the initial position and repeat.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Reverse Machine Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Front Raises
instructions: Sit tall on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't swing the weights.
Keep your back against the pad if there is one.
results.description: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Front Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Side Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Don't shrug.
results.description: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Side Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

results.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs
instructions: Sit tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't roll your shoulders.
Keep your arms straight.
results.description: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Seated Plate Bus Drivers
instructions: Sit tall holding a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, arms extended at shoulder height.
Turn the plate to one side like a steering wheel.
Return to the centre and turn it to the other side.
Keep alternating with your arms at shoulder height.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Sit tall without leaning back.
results.description: Seated Plate Bus Drivers is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

results.name: Seated Plate Front Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a weight plate at its sides in front of your thighs.
Raise the plate in front of you to shoulder height with straight arms.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't lean back.
Use a light plate.
results.description: Seated Plate Front Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Seated Plate Side Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a light plate in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows.
Don't shrug.
results.description: Seated Plate Side Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at face level.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the handles towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your upper back and shoulder muscles to perform the pull, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing down.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the handles upward until your arms are fully extended above your head, forming a straight line with your body.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep tension in the suspension trainer straps throughout the exercise.
Avoid letting your hips sag to maintain proper body alignment.
If you feel strain in your lower back, readjust your position and ensure your core is engaged.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), and lean back slightly with your arms extended.
Engage your upper back and pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and driving them out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.
